The publisher foreground is a very small region at the bottom edge toward the right, whereas the brightest Grad-CAM region lies higher in the lower-right interior. The maximum misses the mask and the mask receives 0.00134% of total attribution, below its 0.15717% uniform-area reference. This is consistent with poor attention to tiny boundary evidence, but does not isolate downsampling as the cause. The 0.790539 score falls below the frozen 0.895234 cutoff. Top-region deletion reduces the defect logit, yet low-attribution deletion reduces it more (2.704260 versus 1.591740); the explanation therefore fails the stronger-than-both-controls sensitivity check. A future study could test boundary-preserving features on new validation groups, without changing this evaluated model.

The original shows subtle left-edge weave/intensity variation; the coarse CAM brightens the lower left and partly overlaps the annotation. Its 21.3191% attribution mass in a 2.69165%-area mask exceeds the uniform reference, but its single maximum remains outside the exact-white mask. Grad-CAM peaks nearby, while the publisher foreground is empty and the explicit patch label is normal. The model score 0.925760 exceeds the frozen 0.895234 cutoff, creating a genuine false positive under the publisher target. The highlight is compatible with sensitivity to a visually distinctive texture feature, but does not establish a real unannotated defect or an incorrect publisher label. Empty-mask overlap and pointing-hit scores are undefined, not zero-quality localisation measures. Top deletion lowers the logit by 2.779529, but low-attribution deletion lowers it more (3.000914); random deletion raises it. This again fails the stronger-than-both-controls check.
